title: Bhutan on a Budget by Road from Siliguri
meta_description: Do Bhutan by road on a budget: Siliguri or NJP to Jaigaon by bus, train or taxi, shoulder months, shared vans, certified 3-star hotels and what is free.
summary: The cheapest way into Bhutan from India is by road: a ₹150–300 bus or a train to Hasimara from Siliguri, then a walk across the gate at Jaigaon into Phuentsholing. Travel in March, early April or November, share one van and guide among four to six people, and use certified 3-star hotels. Indicative, 2026.

sections.heading: Why the road is the budget route
paras: Flying into Paro is quick and the approach over the ridges is famous, but a seat on the small number of Drukair flights from Bagdogra, or on flights from Delhi and Kolkata, costs several times a bus ticket. The road route from Siliguri to Jaigaon is about 155–170 km and four to six hours, through the tea gardens and forests of the Dooars. It costs ₹150–300 by bus.

The road also gives you Phuentsholing, which is a good first night: cheaper hotels than Thimphu, easy food, and a chance to settle permits before the long climb. From Phuentsholing to Thimphu is about 165 km and five to six hours, past the Rinchending checkpoint, Gedu, Chukha and Chhuzom, where the Paro and Thimphu rivers meet beside three chortens.

sections.heading: Siliguri to Jaigaon: bus, train or taxi
paras: Three ways work well. NBSTC and private buses leave Siliguri for Jaigaon through the morning and take five to six hours via Sevoke, Malbazar or Chalsa, Birpara and Hasimara. The train is the comfortable middle option: NJP to Hasimara takes three to four hours, and from Hasimara station it is 18 km, about 30 minutes, to Jaigaon by taxi or auto. A reserved car from Siliguri is the fastest and easiest with luggage and children.

Whatever you choose, aim to reach Jaigaon by early afternoon if you plan to get your permit on arrival, and by mid-morning if you want to drive on to Thimphu the same day. All fares here are indicative, 2026.

sections.heading: Crossing at Jaigaon and Phuentsholing
paras: Indian taxis from Siliguri normally stop at Jaigaon. You walk through the gate to the pedestrian terminal in Phuentsholing with your original passport or Voter ID; Aadhaar is not accepted. If you applied for your Entry Permit online, the check is quick. If not, the permit is issued at the terminal.

Beyond the Rinchending checkpoint, about 5 km up the highway, you need a licensed guide. A Department of Tourism notification of April 2026 restated this for all tourists, and we read it as covering Indians. So your guide and your Bhutan-registered vehicle meet you at Phuentsholing. There are public buses from Phuentsholing to Thimphu for about Nu 250–350, but as a tourist you still need a guide with you, which makes the bus impractical. Check current status before you travel.

On the way home, plan to reach Phuentsholing the evening before you cross. The drive down from Paro is about 150 km and five hours, and the onward road to Siliguri is another four to six hours. Doing both in one day is possible but tiring, and if a landslide holds you up you risk missing a train from Hasimara or NJP. A last night at the border costs one more night of SDF and a hotel, but it buys a relaxed morning, a walk through the Phuentsholing market and an easy crossing back to Jaigaon.

sections.heading: Pick the shoulder months
paras: October and the first half of May are when hotels fill and rates hold firm. You can save on rooms, and often on the van, by travelling either side of the peak. These are the months we suggest for a budget trip by road.
list: March: dry, cold mornings, rhododendrons starting on the passes, Paro Tshechu in some years in late March.
Early April: warmer, clear mornings, hotels still discounting before the May rush.
November: clear skies after the monsoon, cranes arriving in Phobjikha, fewer groups after mid-month.
Late February: close to freezing at night in Thimphu, but clear, quiet and cheap.
Avoid June to August on a tight budget: the Phuentsholing highway can close for hours after landslides, and a lost day still costs you SDF, guide and vehicle.

sections.heading: Share the guide and the van
paras: The guide costs about ₹2,000–3,000 a day and a car with driver about ₹4,500–6,500 a day. A Toyota Hiace for a group costs ₹6,500–9,000 a day. These rates do not change much whether two people use them or six. A couple alone on a six-night trip pays ₹19,500–28,500 each for guide and vehicle. In a group of six, the same line falls to ₹8,500–12,000 each.

So the single best budget move is to travel with friends or another family. If you cannot, ask a Bhutanese operator about fixed-departure group tours. Agree in writing what the daily vehicle rate includes: fuel, the driver's food and stay, and parking. Ask too whether the guide's meals and room are in the daily rate, because on a six-night trip those small extras can add ₹3,000 or more to the bill. Indicative, 2026.

sections.heading: Certified 3-star hotels that work
paras: Tourists must stay in hotels certified by the Department of Tourism at 3-star and above, or in registered homestays and farmhouses. That rules out the cheapest local lodges, but a certified 3-star with breakfast costs about ₹3,000–5,500 a room night, indicative 2026, which is fair for two people.

Three we know: Hotel Druk in Phuentsholing sits on Zhung Lam, about 100 m from the border gate, which saves a taxi on the first and last nights. Hotel Olathang in Paro was built in 1974 for guests at the Fourth King's coronation and sits in pine forest above the town. Hotel Lobesa is a small 3-star at Lobesa, handy for Punakha Dzong and Chimi Lhakhang. Registered farmhouses in Paro and Punakha are a good alternative, and many offer a hot stone bath for ₹1,500–3,000.

sections.heading: Eat where the drivers eat
paras: Hotel buffets cost ₹500–1,000 a head. A local restaurant on a Thimphu side street or by the highway serves red rice, ema datshi, kewa datshi and dal for ₹250–600. Ask your guide where drivers stop for lunch on the Phuentsholing to Thimphu road; it will be cheaper and hotter than the tourist stops. Momos are a cheap snack almost everywhere. Carry a refillable bottle; most hotels will fill it from their filtered supply.

Breakfast is included at almost every certified hotel, so the real food budget is lunch and dinner. If your package includes dinner at the hotel, ask whether you can swap one or two nights for a local restaurant instead; some operators will adjust the price, and it is a better way to taste the country. Tea and suja, the salted butter tea, cost very little in local cafés, and a plate of momos makes a fine light lunch on a sightseeing day.

sections.heading: What is free in Bhutan
paras: Plenty of the best of Bhutan costs nothing beyond the SDF you have already paid. Your guide is with you all day, so use them: they can explain archery scoring, translate at the market and tell you which chortens matter to their family.
list: Watching archery, the national sport since 1971, on a weekend range in Thimphu or Paro; targets stand about 145 m away.
Walking Thimphu's main street and Clock Tower Square in the evening, and noticing there are no traffic lights.
The weekend vegetable market in Thimphu, where you can taste local cheese and see dried chillies by the sack.
Chhuzom, where the Paro and Thimphu rivers meet beside three chortens, on the drive up from Phuentsholing.
The roadside view of the 108 chortens at Dochula on a clear morning.
Tshechu dances in dzong courtyards, which are open to the public; check current status for any tourist ticketing.

faqs.q: How do I go to Bhutan from Siliguri by bus
faqs.a: Take an NBSTC or private bus from Siliguri to Jaigaon, which costs about ₹150–300 a seat and takes five to six hours via Sevoke, Malbazar, Birpara and Hasimara, indicative 2026. Get off at Jaigaon and walk through the gate to the Phuentsholing terminal with your passport or Voter ID. Beyond Rinchending, about 5 km up the road, you need a licensed guide. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: Which railway station is nearest to Bhutan
faqs.a: Hasimara, on the line through the Dooars, is the nearest convenient station to Phuentsholing. It is 18 km, about 30 minutes, from Jaigaon by taxi or auto, which costs about ₹300–600, indicative 2026. Trains from NJP to Hasimara take three to four hours. NJP itself is about 155–170 km from Jaigaon, so Hasimara cuts the road part of the trip to half an hour.

faqs.q: How much does a taxi from Siliguri to Phuentsholing cost
faqs.a: A reserved car from Siliguri or NJP to Jaigaon costs about ₹4,500–6,000, indicative 2026, and takes four to five hours. Indian taxis normally stop at Jaigaon, and you walk across to Phuentsholing. From there your Bhutan-registered tourist vehicle and licensed guide take over. Split among four people, the Siliguri leg costs about ₹1,100–1,500 each, which is fair value with luggage and children.

faqs.q: Can I travel in Bhutan by public bus as a tourist
faqs.a: Public buses run from Phuentsholing to Thimphu for about Nu 250–350, but tourists must be accompanied by a licensed guide beyond Rinchending, as restated by the Department of Tourism in April 2026. That makes public buses impractical for most visitors, because your guide would need to travel with you. For groups, a shared Hiace with a guide is cheaper per head and more flexible. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: What is the cheapest month to visit Bhutan
faqs.a: For a budget trip by road, we suggest late February, March, early April and November. Hotels discount more readily than in October and May, and the roads are dry. June to August can be cheaper still, but landslides on the Phuentsholing highway can cost you a day, and every lost day still costs SDF, guide and vehicle. Check road status before you travel.

faqs.q: Can I stay in cheap hotels in Bhutan
faqs.a: Not the cheapest local lodges. Tourists must stay in Department of Tourism-certified hotels of 3-star and above, or registered homestays and farmhouses. A certified 3-star with breakfast costs about ₹3,000–5,500 a room night, indicative 2026. Phuentsholing hotels are usually a little cheaper than Thimphu and Paro. Registered farmhouses are often good value and include home-cooked meals.

Yes, for a road trip. A night in Phuentsholing lets you finish permits without rushing, start the 165 km drive to Thimphu early, and break the long return. Hotels are often cheaper than in Thimphu, and Hotel Druk sits about 100 m from the border gate. If you only visit Phuentsholing for up to 24 hours and stay below Rinchending, you pay no SDF. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: How long is the drive from Phuentsholing to Thimphu
faqs.a: About 165 km and five to six hours, indicative. The road climbs from about 300 m at Phuentsholing through the Rinchending checkpoint, Gedu and Chukha to Chhuzom, where the Paro and Thimphu rivers meet, then up the valley to Thimphu at about 2,320 m. In the monsoon, June to August, landslides can add hours. Check road status before you travel.

Not if you eat locally. A meal of red rice, ema datshi and dal at a local restaurant costs about ₹250–600, while a hotel buffet costs ₹500–1,000, indicative 2026. Momos are a cheap snack almost everywhere. Ask your guide where drivers eat on the highway; it is usually the cheapest and freshest food on the route.
